universities.name: University of Manchester
universities.headline: Lessons that fit around lectures, from halls in Fallowfield, Victoria Park and the city
facts: The University's halls of residence are spread across three residential campuses: City, Fallowfield and Victoria Park.

Fallowfield is around 2.5km south of the main campus. Victoria Park sits between the City and Fallowfield campuses, about a 15-minute walk from the main campus, and the city centre is about 10 minutes away by bus.
Next to Victoria Park is Rusholme, where a section of Wilmslow Road is known as the Curry Mile.
The University lists a Fallowfield Campus Redevelopment: plans approved by Manchester City Council in January 2024, with first-phase works running until 2027.
universities.travel: Between the Oxford Road campus and Fallowfield the University describes a frequent bus service to and from the city centre, and Victoria Park is about a 15-minute walk from the main campus. A car matters most for the things a bus does not do well: early or late shifts, placements away from the corridor, and getting home with shopping or a bike.
universities.note: Check the University's current parking rules before bringing a car. We cover where you live, not campus permits.
guide: Most first-years live in one of three places, and each suits a different lesson routine. City-campus halls such as Whitworth Park, Weston Hall and Denmark Road put you on or near Oxford Road, so we usually collect you from the halls door or the campus and head south through Rusholme and Withington. From Fallowfield, about 2.5km south of the main campus, you learn on the same suburban roads you are later likely to be tested near. Victoria Park sits in between, about a 15-minute walk from campus, so it works well if you want a pick-up point that is easy to stop at.

Meal times matter if you live in a catered hall. The University lists Ashburne Hall, Dalton-Ellis Hall, Hulme Hall and St Anselm Hall as catered. In Fallowfield, breakfast runs from 7.30am to 9.30am and dinner from 5.15pm to 7.15pm on weekdays, so a late-afternoon or after-dinner lesson avoids clashing with the dining room. Fallowfield is also the site of the University's campus redevelopment (first-phase works until 2027), so ask your instructor to meet you on a quiet street that is easy to stop on.
universities.fit: Tell us your lecture days and whether you live in a catered hall. We can aim for pick-ups outside meal times and teaching hours.
faqs: Which University of Manchester halls are catered?
The University lists Ashburne Hall, Dalton-Ellis Hall, Hulme Hall and St Anselm Hall as its catered halls. The other halls are self-catered.
How far is Fallowfield from the main campus?
The University describes the Fallowfield campus as around 2.5km south of the main campus. Victoria Park is between the two, about a 15-minute walk from the main campus.
Where do you pick up from if I live in Fallowfield or Victoria Park?
From your halls, your house or the nearest safe stopping place. Give us your full postcode on the form and we match you with an instructor close by.

universities.name: Manchester Metropolitan University
universities.headline: Lessons from your halls, Birley or All Saints, around your timetable
facts: Manchester Met's own hall comparison table lists 19 halls, run either by the university or by partners (Unite Students, IQ Students, Vita Students and Mezzino).
The table gives journey times from each hall to the Business School and the Brooks Building.
Most halls list journeys of under 15 minutes. Brook Hall, Chandos House, Ropemaker Court and Wilmslow Park each list at least one journey of 20 minutes or more.
Parkway Gate and Artisan Heights also appear in the University of Manchester's list of halls.
universities.travel: Most halls sit close to campus, so lessons are usually about getting you test-ready on a regular weekly slot rather than about commuting. Students in the further-out halls have the most to gain from a licence, because longer journeys are the ones a car shortens.
sources: Manchester Met: choose your university accommodation (hall comparison table)
universities.note: We are independent of Manchester Met. Hall details come from the university's own pages and may change.
guide: Manchester Met has a wider spread of accommodation than most universities, with 19 halls across its own blocks and partner providers. Ten are run by the university itself, including the five Birley halls (Dale, Dunham, Naylor, Vine and Warde), Archway, Briarfield, Cavendish, Needham Court and Oxford Court. The other nine are partner halls run by Unite Students, IQ Students, Vita Students and Mezzino. If you are in one of the 12-person Birley houses (Dale, Naylor or Warde), agree one clear pick-up point with your instructor so you are not hunting for the right door.

Distance is where a licence earns its keep. Most halls list journeys of under 15 minutes to the Business School and Brooks Building, but Brook Hall, Chandos House, Ropemaker Court and Wilmslow Park each list at least one journey of 20 minutes or more. Students in those halls have the most to gain from learning early, because a longer commute is the journey a car shortens.
universities.fit: Give us your hall's postcode and your teaching days, and we will match you with an instructor close to your door.
faqs: Which Manchester Met halls are run by the university itself?
From the university's hall comparison table: Archway, Birley Dale, Birley Dunham, Birley Naylor, Birley Vine, Birley Warde, Briarfield, Cavendish, Needham Court and Oxford Court.
Which halls have the longest journeys to campus?
Manchester Met's table lists at least one journey of 20 minutes or more for Brook Hall, Chandos House, Ropemaker Court and Wilmslow Park.
Do Manchester Met students share halls with other universities?
Parkway Gate and Artisan Heights appear in both Manchester Met's and the University of Manchester's hall lists.

universities.name: University of Salford
universities.headline: Lessons from Peel Park, Frederick Road and MediaCityUK
facts: The University of Salford is across three campuses: Peel Park (University of Salford, 43 Crescent, Salford M5 4WT), Frederick Road (Frederick Road Campus, Broad Street, Salford M6 6PU) and MediaCity (B4, Orange Tower, Salford Quays M50 2HE).
Salford Crescent station is between the Peel Park and Frederick Road campuses. The University warns not to mistake Salford Central for Salford Crescent, which leaves a 20-minute walk.

Buses 8, 35, 36, 37, 38, 50, 67, 100, V1 and V2 stop at The Crescent outside the Peel Park entrance. Students and staff can travel free on the 50 bus from Monday to Friday by showing their University ID.
University of Salford students can get a 50% discount on adult season tickets through Northern's higher education scheme.

For bikes, the University lists over 400 secure shelter spaces and a 300-space Cycle Hub at MediaCity run by Transport for Greater Manchester. Lime e-scooters run under a scheme licensed by Salford City Council.
On parking, the University says you must hold a valid parking session, a pay and display ticket or a Blue Badge when you park on its campuses.
universities.travel: Salford is well served by trains, buses and bikes, so the case for a licence is less about getting to lectures and more about everything else: placements and jobs that finish late, trips home, and the freedom to work or live further out. A licence can also open up job options after graduation.
sources: University of Salford: travel to the University
universities.note: Salford has no centre of its own in the DVSA Manchester group, so your instructor will advise which test centre suits your route.
guide: Salford's three campuses are close enough to link but different enough to plan around. Peel Park (43 Crescent, M5 4WT) and Frederick Road (Broad Street, M6 6PU) sit either side of Salford Crescent station, while MediaCity (Orange Tower, Salford Quays, M50 2HE) is further away. For lessons, that means three natural pick-up zones: around the Crescent, around Frederick Road and Broad Street, and around the Quays. Tell us which one you live nearest to and we will aim for an instructor already working that patch.

Because the 50 bus is free for students Monday to Friday and several routes stop at The Crescent, many Salford students manage without a car during term. A licence is most useful in the gaps: late finishes, placements away from the bus corridors, trips home and jobs after graduation. If you do bring a car, note the University's rule that you must hold a valid parking session, a pay and display ticket or a Blue Badge when parking on campus.
universities.fit: Tell us whether your lectures are at Peel Park, Frederick Road or MediaCity, and which days you finish early.
faqs: Which buses stop at the University of Salford's Peel Park campus?

The University lists buses 8, 35, 36, 37, 38, 50, 67, 100, V1 and V2 as stopping at The Crescent, outside the Peel Park entrance. For Frederick Road, any of those except the 67 and 100 take you closer.
Is the 50 bus free for Salford students?
The University says students and staff can travel free on the 50 bus from Monday to Friday by showing their University ID.
What is the difference between Salford Crescent and Salford Central?
Salford Crescent station is between the Peel Park and Frederick Road campuses. The University warns that mistaking Salford Central for Salford Crescent leaves a 20-minute walk.

universities.name: University of Greater Manchester (formerly the University of Bolton)
universities.headline: Lessons for Bolton students, from campus or Orlando Village
facts: The University of Bolton now trades as the University of Greater Manchester, after a regulatory approval process that ITV News reported in December 2024.
The campus is on Deane Road, Bolton, BL3 5AB, a short walk from Bolton's rail and coach stations.
The university says visitor parking on campus is limited and recommends the Wellington Street Pay and Display car park.

Orlando Village, the student accommodation featured on the university's accommodation page, is a 10-minute walk from the main campus and lists car parking, a free campus bus and 24/7 security on site.
The university's student union is called the Greater Manchester Students' Union.
universities.travel: Bolton is compact, but many students live in the town's surrounding areas or travel in from Bury, Wigan and further afield. A licence is useful for placements, commuting to work in Greater Manchester and getting home late.
sources: University of Greater Manchester: getting in touch (campus address and parking)
University of Greater Manchester: accommodation (Orlando Village)
ITV News: University of Bolton changes its name to University of Greater Manchester
universities.note: We are independent of the university. Name and campus details are from its own website.
guide: If you knew this place as the University of Bolton, the name has changed but the campus has not: it is still on Deane Road, Bolton (BL3 5AB), a short walk from the town's rail and coach stations. That central position helps lessons. Your instructor can collect you from the campus or from Orlando Village, which the university's accommodation page describes as a 10-minute walk from the main campus, with car parking available and a free campus bus.

Visitor parking on campus is limited, and the university recommends the Wellington Street Pay and Display car park. If you will bring a car as a learner or a new driver, plan your parking before your first week. Many students also live in Bolton's surrounding areas or travel in from places such as Bury and Wigan, so tell us your home postcode as well as your campus.
universities.fit: Tell us if you live at Orlando Village or commute in from another town, and we will plan your pick-up around that.
faqs: Is the University of Greater Manchester the same as the University of Bolton?
Yes. The University of Bolton now trades as the University of Greater Manchester, after the regulatory approval process that ITV News reported in December 2024.
Where should I park when visiting the campus?
The university says visitor parking on campus is limited and recommends the Wellington Street Pay and Display car park.
How far is Orlando Village from the main campus?
The university's accommodation page describes Orlando Village as a 10-minute walk from the main university campus.

colleges.name: The Manchester College
campuses: Centre of Excellence for Medical Sciences
colleges.headline: Lessons for adult learners across all six Manchester College campuses
facts: The Manchester College lists campuses in three areas: Central Manchester (Centre of Excellence for Medical Sciences, Nicholls Campus and City Campus Manchester), South Manchester (Wythenshawe Campus) and North and East Manchester (Harpurhey and Openshaw campuses).
The college has a dedicated Adult Learners section and a published list of adult courses.
Its campuses are spread across Greater Manchester, so where you learn to drive often depends on which campus you attend and where you live, not on one central point.
colleges.travel: Adult learners at a large multi-campus college often fit study around work or caring. We ask for your availability on the booking form and match you with an instructor whose diary fits, including evenings and weekends where an instructor has them.
guide: The Manchester College is not one site but six, and where you learn to drive naturally follows which one you attend and where you live. In central Manchester there are City Campus, Nicholls Campus and the Centre of Excellence for Medical Sciences. In the north and east there are Harpurhey and Openshaw. In the south there is Wythenshawe. We already teach around Harpurhey, Openshaw, Wythenshawe and the city centre, so most learners can be matched with an instructor who knows their area.

As an adult learner you may be balancing study with shifts, caring or a family. Say so on the form. Lessons that finish where your day continues, rather than back at a campus you do not need to visit, are usually easier to keep up with week after week.
colleges.fit: Tell us which campus you study at and which days you work, so lessons do not clash with either.
faqs: Which campuses does The Manchester College have?

Its locations page lists City Campus Manchester, Nicholls Campus and the Centre of Excellence for Medical Sciences in Central Manchester, Wythenshawe Campus in South Manchester, and Harpurhey Campus and Openshaw Campus in North and East Manchester.
Does The Manchester College have an adult learners section?
Yes. The college has a dedicated adult learners section and a published list of adult courses.
Do you teach near Wythenshawe, Harpurhey and Openshaw?
Yes. We have local pages for all three, and we match you with an instructor close to your pick-up postcode.

colleges.name: Trafford & Stockport College Group
colleges.headline: Lessons for Trafford College, Stockport College and Cheadle College learners
facts: The Trafford & Stockport College Group was formed when Stockport College and Trafford College merged, and includes Trafford College, Stockport College, Cheadle College and Marple Sixth Form College.
Trafford College has campuses in Altrincham and Stretford. Cheadle College is on Cheadle Road, Cheadle Hulme, Stockport, SK8 5HA.
The group runs adult and professional skills university centre open events showcasing courses across Stockport and Trafford.
colleges.travel: The group spans two boroughs, so the right instructor depends on where you live and study. Tell us your pick-up postcode and we match you with someone local.
guide: This group spans two boroughs, which makes it unusual. Trafford College has campuses in Altrincham and Stretford. Stockport College and Cheadle College (Cheadle Road, Cheadle Hulme, SK8 5HA) are in Stockport borough, and the group also includes Marple Sixth Form College. We teach all around those places, from Altrincham, Sale and Urmston to Stockport and Cheadle.

Two DVSA test centres in the Manchester group sit in these boroughs: Sale in Trafford and Bredbury in the Stockport area. Sale had a 51.4% pass rate in 2025/26 and Bredbury 56.0%, the highest of all eight Manchester centres. Pass rates reflect who takes tests there, not route difficulty, but if you live between the two, your instructor can talk you through which suits your routes and the earliest available dates.
colleges.fit: Say whether you are at Altrincham, Stretford, Stockport or Cheadle, and what time you finish.
faqs: Which colleges are in the Trafford & Stockport College Group?
Trafford College, Stockport College, Cheadle College and Marple Sixth Form College, according to the group's website.
Where is Cheadle College?
Cheadle College is on Cheadle Road, Cheadle Hulme, Stockport, SK8 5HA.
Which DVSA test centres are in Trafford and Stockport?
The DVSA's Manchester group includes Sale (in Trafford) and Bredbury (in the Stockport area).
